title: Space Tech Briefing — October 17, 2026
summary:
Good morning, space enthusiasts! It's Friday, October 17, 2026, and you're tuned into your essential daily dose of cosmic news! Let's dive straight into the incredible developments shaping our universe.

First up, as we look forward to future breakthroughs, let's cast our eyes back to a monumental journey nearing its grand finale. The BepiColombo mission, a joint venture between ESA and JAXA, is almost at Mercury! After an incredible eight-year voyage, covering nearly 10 billion kilometers, this intrepid probe is set to enter orbit around the scorching hot planet on November 21st. Get ready for some groundbreaking science from the solar system's innermost world!

And speaking of incredible achievements, we're still buzzing from the return of ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot! Just a few days ago, on October 13th, she held her first press conference at the European Astronaut Centre in Cologne, following her record-breaking mission aboard the International Space Station with Crew-12. ESA's Director of Human and Robotic Exploration, Daniel Neuenschwander, highlighted her phenomenal accomplishments: Sophie completed the longest stay ever for an ESA astronaut, spending an astounding 237 days in space! Not only that, she became the first ESA astronaut in two decades to perform *three* spacewalks on her very first mission. And, to top it all off, she's the first from ESA's 2022 astronaut class to have flown to space. What an absolute trailblazer!

That's all for your Morning Briefing on this fantastic Friday. Keep your eyes on the skies and your ears peeled for more space news right here. Have a stellar day!
